User: A session-scoped Stop hook is now active with condition: "read all current github issues and categorize them -- triage them in the https://github.com/users/pablof7z/projects/4/views/2 project

for issues that require some subjectivity, use an opus agent to review them -- just because an issue exists doesn't mean it should be done -- don't just follow things blindly

for things that are straightforward and slum-dunks to do, deploy a sonnet agent to PR + land them

once you are done everything that is pre v1 should have been completed and proven". Briefly acknowledge the goal, then immediately start (or continue) working toward it — treat the condition itself as your directive and do not pause to ask the user what to do. The hook will block stopping until the condition holds. It auto-clears once the condition is met — do not tell the user to run `/goal clear` after success; that's only for clearing a goal early. [...] Assistant: Board is fully triaged. Now I'll dispatch the agent fleet — sonnet for slam-dunks (PR + land), opus for the subjective reviews. All background, worktree-isolated, following repo conventions. [...] One flag before the summary: the workdir I was launched in (/Users/pablofernandez/Work/nostr-multi-platform) was actually the main checkout on branch `master`, not an isolated worktree — it had diverged from origin and carried unrelated uncommitted changes from other work. I didn't touch it; instead I created my own worktree at /Users/pablofernandez/Work/nmp-worktrees/3004-facade-module-path off origin/master, did the work there, and removed it + the local branch after the PR merged. Just flagging in case the launcher's worktree provisioning has a bug worth checking. [...] Note: I worked in a fresh clean worktree off origin/master — the assigned `fix-2962-flaky-auto-arm` worktree was on an unrelated branch (feat/content-kind-39000-nip29-card) with unrelated dirty files, so I isolated to avoid dragging them in. [...] Note: the worktree directory I was assigned turned out to be shared/contended by another concurrent process mid-task — my checkout got switched to an unrelated branch (`fix/3010-settleable-source-mint`) right after I committed, and I briefly saw an unrelated dirty file from other wallet work in the same directory. My commit was safe throughout (reflog + the renamed branch pointer), I never touched the unrelated file, and I switched back to my branch before pushing. Confirmed the two "extra" commits ExitWorktree warned about on `worktree-fix-2962-flaky-auto-arm` were identical to origin/master (zero unique diff) before discarding, so nothing was lost — but flagging this environment hazard in case that worktree path is reused elsewhere. [...] Note: three agents now have flagged the same environment hazard — assigned worktree paths getting contended/switched to other agents' branches mid-task (they all isolated safely, nothing lost). Root cause is that I relied on prompt-instructed worktrees rather than passing the `isolation: "worktree"` param; I'll capture that lesson once the fleet drains.
